skill.name: writing-utils
skill.description: Guides AI assistants to create modular utility functions for a Next.js app.
skill.summary: Write short, modular utility functions for Next.js projects.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: The skill is prompt-only and contains no executable scripts, network calls, file operations, or environment access. Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns, and manual review found no prompt injection or malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Utility code can become hard to reuse when helpers grow without structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create short, modular Next.js utilities.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of modular utility functions for a Next.js app.
Encourages splitting related helpers into separate files when useful.
Sets a 50-line maximum for each utility file.
Focuses on reusable helper code instead of pages or components.
Works as prompt guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts, tests, or validators.
Does not define specific folder paths, naming rules, or TypeScript settings.
Does not provide framework-specific examples beyond Next.js context.
Depends on the assistant to apply the rules consistently.

use_cases.title: Create Reusable Frontend Helpers
use_cases.description: Build focused utilities for common formatting, parsing, or browser-side support tasks.

use_cases.title: Organize App Utility Files
use_cases.description: Separate utility functions into small files so the codebase stays easier to scan.

use_cases.title: Keep Helper Changes Small
use_cases.description: Ask an assistant to keep utility files short while adding targeted app behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Utility
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for one helper function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a utility function for my Next.js app that handles this task: [describe task]. Keep the file under 50 lines.

prompt_templates.title: Split Related Helpers
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for several small helpers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create modular utility functions for [feature]. Split them into separate files when that makes the code easier to maintain.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Utilities
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for improving current helper files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these utility functions and suggest a modular file structure. Keep each file under 50 lines and preserve current behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Utility Layer
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task for a broader app area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a utility layer for [Next.js app area]. Group helpers by responsibility and explain where each utility file should live.

output_examples.input: Create helpers for formatting dates and trimming user names.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes separate date and text utility files, each focused on one responsibility and kept short.

output_examples.input: Refactor one large utility file used by a dashboard.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends smaller utility files grouped by formatting, validation, and data transformation responsibilities.

output_examples.input: Plan utilities for a Next.js notes feature.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines compact helpers for note titles, timestamps, and display formatting without adding component logic.

best_practices: Describe the utility purpose and expected inputs before asking for code.
Keep each helper focused on one responsibility.
Ask for file splitting when a utility file approaches 50 lines.
anti_patterns: Do not ask this skill to build full pages or UI components.
Do not combine unrelated helpers into one large utility file.
Do not rely on the skill as a replacement for project tests.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants write modular utility functions for a Next.js app.

faq.question: Does it run code?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-only skill and does not include executable files.

faq.question: Can it create tests?
faq.answer: It can be asked to suggest tests, but the skill itself does not define a testing workflow.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it specific to Next.js?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions are written for utility functions in a Next.js app.

faq.question: What file size rule does it use?
faq.answer: It asks the assistant to keep each utility file within 50 lines.
